messages:
Sam: Heads up — after last night's RBAC role rename + key rotation, we're seeing Okta SCIM deprovisioning fail for a subset of customers with 403s. I see KMS decrypt errors in the audit logs. Anyone digging?
Irene: I started looking. 403s come from our provisioning endpoint after IdP returns a JWE assertion. Our provisoner logs show JWE decrypt failures: 'jwe: decryption failed' and a KMS error 'key not found' for kid 'alias/provisioner-old'.
Priya: Can you paste the exact log lines?
Irene: Sure — snippet below:
```
2026-03-20T02:28:12Z scim-provisioner[prod-2] ERROR failed to decrypt assertion; err="jwe: decryption failed" kid="alias/provisioner-old"
2026-03-20T02:28:12Z scim-provisioner[prod-2] WARN incoming provisioning op="deprovision" status=403 user=acct-*** org=org-14
2026-03-20T02:28:12Z kms-client ERROR GetKey("alias/provisioner-old") -> NotFound
```
Morgan: From audit-log, the KMS rotation ran at 02:15 UTC and removed the old alias as part of the post-rotate cleanup. Looks like the provisioning service still signs/encrypts with the old kid in some queued jobs.
Sam: We rotated the key but the rollout was supposed to update all provisoner instances. Looks like staging/prod drifted. Who applied the alias cleanup?
deploy-bot: Rotation run by infra-ops at 02:15 UTC. Post-rotation cleanup step removed alias 'alias/provisioner-old' from KMS.
Priya: Mitigation ideas: 1) re-add the old alias as a pointer to the new key (fast) 2) pause the provisioning consumer and drain/backfill after we re-encrypt payloads (safer) 3) roll back key rotation (more blast radius).
Irene: I paused the provisioning consumer for deprovision events for affected partitions (paused at 02:40 UTC). Will keep paused until we confirm a fix.
Morgan: I can re-create alias mapping (alias -> key-id) in KMS but need infra approval to change key metadata.
Sam: @infra-ops / @security-leads can you approve re-adding the alias as a temporary fix? We need to restore customer deprovisioning quickly but with audit trace.
Morgan: If approved I will add alias and add a 1-hour retention tag to remind us to remove it after verification. Also will record an audit entry.
Priya: Also note we should avoid reprocessing any deprovision ops twice — when we resume the consumer we should mark in-flight ops as in-progress and dedupe by op-id.
Irene: Affected tenants: ~14 orgs attempted deprovision between 02:28-02:36 UTC. No large-scale data loss — ops were rejected, not executed. I'll DM infra the list.
auditor-bot: Incident IN-2026-114 created: "SCIM deprovision 403 caused by KMS alias cleanup"
Sam: Postmortem action items (short):
- Add validation step to key rotation runbook to verify alias propagation to all provisioning instances.
- Update RBAC/role-rename playbook to ensure services re-pick credentials before alias removal.
- Add a preflight check that queries KMS for expected kids used by queued jobs.
- Add a tracing tag to SCIM ops to make in-flight signing kid visible in logs.
Priya: I'll open a tiny PR to the rotation playbook with the preflight verification checks.
Irene: For now, once alias is restored and we validate, I'll re-enable consumer and slowly ramp at 10% then 100%.
Sam: Thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated when alias is re-added or if infra declines.
Morgan: Alias re-added at 03:05 UTC and tagged. Re-enabling consumer once we confirm KMS GetKey succeeds for both kids.
Irene: Confirmed: provisioning decrypts succeed for test tenants. Resuming consumer at 03:18 UTC, will monitor error rate.
Sam: Good. Please paste timeline + customer list into the incident ticket and assign owners for the follow-ups.
